sources.entry: DePay - Accept Web3 Payments directly into your wallet peer-to-peer. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: A JavaScript widget library (npm package @depay/widgets) that adds wallet-to-wallet Web3 crypto payment, wallet connect, login, and token/NFT selector dialogs to a website or dApp.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a Payment widget that lets a site accept crypto tokens across several blockchains (EVM chains and Solana) directly into the seller's wallet, configured either through a managed integration ID or inline with an "accept" list of blockchain, token, amount and receiver. It supports fixed fiat-currency amounts, selectable amounts, extra fees, token allow/deny lists, wallet sorting and filtering, custom styling and CSS injection. It also includes a Connect widget that returns a connected account and wallet, a Login widget that has users sign a message and verifies the signature via a backend endpoint or custom recover function, and a Select widget for picking tokens or NFT collections. Lifecycle callbacks (before, sent, succeeded, validated, failed, critical, error) are available, though the README discourages relying on client-side callbacks.
use_cases: accept crypto payments on a website
add wallet connect button to a dApp
wallet signature login with web3 wallet
select token or NFT in a dialog
notable: Supports both EVM and Solana via separate packages (@depay/widgets-evm, @depay/widgets-svm)
Managed integrations configured remotely through app.depay.com, or unmanaged inline configuration
Multi-blockchain payment routing with automatic network switching
Optional fiat-denominated amounts with local currency display
Login widget with signature verification via backend endpoint
caveats: Client-side callbacks and flow management are explicitly not recommended; device handovers and app-to-app transitions can break them
Unmanaged configurations provide no server-side callbacks or integrations; managed integrations are needed for those
Requires SSR guarding (load only on client side) in frameworks like Next.js
Managed integration configuration depends on the external app.depay.com service
